facts.label: A1
facts.text:
[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] The normalized bracket is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented
R1, R2, or R3 move ([[lem-kauffman-bracket-curl-and-writhe-correction]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two ambient-isotopic regular oriented link
diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] Every oriented link may be moved off the point at infinity into $\mathbb R^3$,
and the directions giving regular projections are dense in $S^2$
([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]],
[[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]).

steps.text: A closed braid diagram has one crossing for each letter in a finite Artin word and no crossings at its closure arcs. Each positive generator contributes $+1$ to writhe by [F2]. In the reflected inverse half twist, the over- and under-strands exchange while their oriented projected tangent vectors retain their respective directions; exchanging the two vectors negates their determinant, so each inverse generator contributes $-1$. Summing over the word and using the homomorphism in [F3] and the finite word representation in [F8] gives $$\operatorname{wr}(\widehat\beta)=e(\beta).$$ [F2, F3, F8, algebra]

facts.label: A1
facts.text:
[A1] Full AC means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] Full AC implies countable choice
([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The positive Artin half twist has determinant crossing sign $+1$; the
opposite reflected half twist exchanges over and under and has sign $-1$
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] The braid exponent sum is additive, with $e(\sigma_i)=1$ and
$e(\sigma_i^{-1})=-1$
([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] For every braid closure, the normalized bracket satisfies
$$f_{\widehat\beta}(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(\widehat\beta)} \langle\widehat\beta\rangle,$$
and its value is independent of the regular diagram under AC$ _\omega$
([[thm-normalized-bracket-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] For every $n$-braid, the raw bracket has the trace expression
$$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta)) \big|_{v=A^{-4},\,z=-1/(A^{-4}+1)},\qquad \delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$$
([[lem-hecke-bracket-trace-dictionary-and-local-descent]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] The library Jones value is invariant under braid equivalence and Markov
moves under full AC, and is given by the trace formula in the Statement
([[thm-the-hecke-trace-construction-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]],
[[def-temperley-lieb-quotient-and-jones-specialization]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] Every nonempty oriented link has a braid closure under full AC
([[thm-alexanders-closed-braid-theorem]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

facts.label: F8
facts.text:
[F8] Every element of $B_n$ is represented by a finite word in the Artin
generators and their inverses; each letter is one geometric half twist or its
opposite, and the closure joins the braid endpoints
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

steps.text: For a state with $k$ B-smoothings, the smoothed braid is the closure of a stack with $k$ copies of $e_1$ and $3-k$ identity layers, because each A-smoothing is $I$ by [F2]. If $k=0$, the identity closure has two circles by [F3]. If $k\ge1$, the first $e_1$ connects the two closing arcs into one circle; each additional $e_1$ contributes one removed loop by $e_1^2=\delta e_1$ in [F4]. Thus the state has $k$ circles. There are $\binom{3}{k}$ states with $k$ B-smoothings, each with weight $A^{3-2k}\delta^{|S|-1}$. The complete state table is $$\begin{array}{c|c|c|l} k & \text{states} & \text{circles} & \text{total contribution} \\ \hline 0 & 1 & 2 & A^3\delta \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & 3A \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 3A^{-1}\delta \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & A^{-3}\delta^2 \end{array}$$ Each term follows from [F1] and the circle counts in [F3–F4]. [F1, F2, F3, F4, construct]

steps.text: Substituting $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ into the table gives $$\begin{aligned} \langle D_+\rangle &=A^3\delta+3A+3A^{-1}\delta+A^{-3}\delta^2\\ &=(-A^5-A)+3A+(-3A-3A^{-3}) +(A+2A^{-3}+A^{-7})\\ &=A^{-7}-A^{-3}-A^5. \end{aligned}$$ The braid has three positive crossings, so [F5] gives $\operatorname{wr}(D_+)=3$. Therefore $$f_{D_+}(A)=(-A^3)^{-3}(A^{-7}-A^{-3}-A^5) =A^{-4}+A^{-12}-A^{-16}=t+t^3-t^4.$$ By [F6], this is the library Jones value. [F1, F5, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

steps.text: Mirroring keeps the projection and swaps over and under. To return the over-strand to the source chart's southwest-to-northeast position, rotate the local chart through a positive quarter-turn; this exchanges the top/bottom and left/right pairings. Thus the A- and B-smoothings interchange, so state-by-state $\langle D_-\rangle(A)=\langle D_+\rangle(A^{-1})$. The determinant sign changes sign when the over and under tangent vectors are exchanged, hence $\operatorname{wr}(D_-)=-3$ by [F5]. It follows directly that $f_{D_-}(A)=f_{D_+}(A^{-1})=t^{-1}+t^{-3}-t^{-4}$, and [F6] identifies this with $V_{D_-}(t)$. By [F7], the crossing-free one-circle diagram has one state with one circle and writhe $0$, so its raw bracket is $1$ and [F6] gives $V_U(t)=1$. [F1, F5, F6, F7, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] The algorithm enumerates every smoothing state once and adds
$A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}$, with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$
([[alg-kauffman-bracket-state-sum]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] In the declared chart, a positive braid crossing has operator
$C_1=AI+A^{-1}e_1$, with $I$ the two through strands and $e_1$ the top-cap,
bottom-cup diagram ([[lem-hecke-bracket-trace-dictionary-and-local-descent]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] The Temperley–Lieb closure trace assigns $\delta^{c(D)}$ to a basis
diagram, where $c(D)$ counts circles after joining corresponding top and
bottom endpoints. The closure of $I$ has two circles, and the closure of
$e_1$ has one ([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] Stacking satisfies $e_1^2=\delta e_1$
([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] Each positive Artin half twist has crossing sign $+1$; mirroring swaps
over and under and negates the determinant sign
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] The normalized bracket of every nonempty oriented link equals the
library Jones specialization after $t=A^{-4}$
([[thm-bracket-state-sum-matches-library-jones-specialization]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] The closure of the identity one-strand braid is the crossing-free
one-component unknot ([[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

facts.label: F1

[F1] A crossing-free one-component diagram has one state with one circle and
bracket $(-A^2-A^{-2})^{1-1}=1$
([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] Adding a positive type-I kink multiplies the raw bracket by $-A^3$
([[lem-kauffman-bracket-curl-and-writhe-correction]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] An oriented type-I kink is an allowed local Reidemeister replacement and
each such local replacement is realized by an ambient isotopy of the oriented
link ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]],
[[lem-each-oriented-reidemeister-move-is-realized-by-ambient-isotopy]]).

steps.text: For an annular link $L:C\hookrightarrow\mathcal A\times(-1,1)$, write its annular projection as $g:C\to\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$. Since $L(C)$ is compact in the interior, its projection has positive distance from $\partial\mathcal A$. Fix an auxiliary smooth embedding $x:C\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^3$. Perturb the two coordinates of $g$ by a finite-dimensional family of polynomials of degree at most five in $x$, multiplied by a smooth cutoff supported in $\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$ and equal to one near $g(C)$. At any three distinct points $x_1,x_2,x_3$, the polynomials $p_i(x)=\prod_{j\ne i}\lVert x-x_j\rVert^2$ vanish to first order at the other two points and are nonzero at $x_i$; multiplying by affine functions therefore prescribes independently the value and first derivative of both projected coordinates at these points. Thus the family is a submersion on every one-, two-, and three-point first-jet space. [A1, F4, given, construct]

steps.text: Apply [F4] to the derivative-zero stratum, the pair-equality diagonal, the nontransverse-pair stratum, and the triple-equality diagonal. The derivative-zero stratum has codimension two on the one-dimensional source, so it is avoided. Pair equality has codimension two on the two-dimensional distinct-pair source and is transverse, hence gives isolated double points; tangency imposes one additional independent equation, so its codimension is three and it is avoided. Triple equality has codimension four on the three-dimensional distinct-triple source, so it is avoided. A sufficiently small good parameter keeps the curve in the annulus and keeps $(g_a(x),L_3(x))$ embedded, because the original embedding is compact and embedding is open in the $C^1$ topology. The parameter path supplies an isotopy of the framed link, with its framing transported along the annuli. [A1, F4, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

steps.text: The transverse double pairs are finite. Immersion gives, near each point of the compact source, a source arc on which the projection is injective; finitely many such arcs exclude double pairs near the diagonal in $C\times C$. Away from that diagonal, the double-pair set is closed in a compact set and is discrete by transversality, hence finite. This proves the annular regular-diagram assertion. For a link in $S^3$, choose orientations on its finitely many components, move it off $\infty$, and apply [F1]. [F1, step 2.1, algebra]

steps.text: For an isotopy in $X$, reparametrize it to be constant near its endpoints and choose regular endpoint diagrams using steps 1.1, 2.1, and 3.1. Regard $X$ as an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ by the annulus-product coordinates. Its compact isotopy track has positive distance from the boundary of $X$. Apply [F3] with a perturbation smaller than this distance and fixed near the endpoints. Every exceptional event and every regular interval then remains in $X$; by [F3] its projected annular diagrams differ by a finite sequence of R1, R2, R3, and planar isotopies in disks of $\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$. For isotopies in $S^3$, [F2] gives the corresponding finite sequence after orienting the components and transporting those orientations. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, given]

steps.text: A planar isotopy transports the blackboard strip continuously. In R2 and R3 the participating strips deform inside the move ball without a full rotation of the normal direction. In an A-type R1 move the blackboard strip gains one full twist, and in the opposite B-type move it loses one; this is the local curl convention in [F6]. Since the framed link isotopy transports the specified annulus without changing its homotopy class, the recorded integer correction changes by the negative of that blackboard turn. Thus the move sequence preserves the framed isotopy class, and all framing changes in the statement are exact. [F5, F6, step 4.1, given, algebra] ∎

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] Countable choice is the assertion that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] A regular oriented link diagram is an immersion with finitely many transverse double points, no triple points, and over/under and orientation data; every oriented link in $S^3$ has a regular projection under countable choice ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Under countable choice, two regular oriented diagrams in $S^3$ represent equivalent oriented links exactly when a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves connects them ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

facts.label: F3

steps.text: The inverse of the positive crossing is its negative crossing: stacking them creates a type-II bigon, which cancels by regular isotopy. steps.text: When the positive crossing is followed by a cup-cap, the two branches belong to the same bent strand. Relative to their downward braid orientations exactly one branch reverses, so its determinant self-crossing sign is negative. Thus $G_iE_i=E_iG_i=a^{-1}E_i=\rho^{-1}E_i$; the negative crossing gives the positive self-curl and coefficient $a=\rho$. For $E_iG_{i+1}E_i$, follow the surviving strand from the top position $i+2$: it traverses the crossing from position $i+2$ to $i+1$, turns along the lower cup to position $i$, returns up the uncrossed strand at position $i$ to the upper cap, and traverses the other crossing branch from $i+1$ to $i+2$. Both encounters are downward in the crossing disk, so the self-crossing has positive determinant sign and gives $aE_i=\rho E_i$. The index $i-1$ case is the same trace with the positions reversed. Stacking $E_i$ twice creates a disjoint trivial circle and leaves $E_i$, so $E_i^2=dE_i=\delta E_i$. The self-curl sign after a cup is distinct from the positive self-curl formed by closing a positive two-strand braid. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

steps.text: Use source coordinates $(u,v)$ with their standard positive orientation and positive projection coordinates $(t,x)$ on the braid box. For $h>0$, the map $(t,x)=(v,-2hu)$ has determinant $2h>0$. It sends the source over direction $(1,1)$ to $(1,-2h)$ and the source under direction $(-1,1)$ to $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is $4h>0$. The source left/right pairs have constant $u$, hence constant braid position $x$ and give the through pairing $I$; the source top/bottom pairs have constant $v$, hence constant braid time $t$ and give the cup-cap $e_i$. The displayed page coordinates $(x,t)$ reverse the positive projection orientation; their visual quarter-turn is not the orientation comparison. Thus the A/B crossing expansion is $C_i=AI+A^{-1}e_i$. Its inverse is $C_i^{-1}=A^{-1}I+Ae_i$, since their product is $I+(A^2+A^{-2}+\delta)e_i=I$. By [A1] and [F8]–[F9], the categorical ribbon trace is the framed tangle evaluation of this braid closure, and that evaluator is monoidal with the stated crossing and duality maps. Expanding a braid word into the two smoothing choices therefore gives the bracket weights in [F4]. Because the closure has $n\ge1$ strands, each complete smoothing is a nonempty closed 1-manifold, hence a union of at least one circle. Its categorical value is $\delta^{|S|}$ by monoidality in [F8] and the loop value [F2], whereas the bracket state sum uses $\delta^{|S|-1}$; the extra single factor is independent of the state. Thus $t_n(\beta)=\delta\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F8, F9, step 1.1, given, algebra]

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The fundamental module has the displayed positive braiding matrix $c_{V,V}$ and scalar twist $-A^3\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[def-quantum-sl2-fundamental-ribbon-module]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] Its self-dual evaluation and coevaluation are the maps $B,U$ whose closed-loop value is $\delta$ ([[def-quantum-sl2-fundamental-ribbon-module]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The ribbon evaluation of the $V$-colored closed braid is the left categorical trace $t_n(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_{V^{\otimes n}}\rho_n(\beta))$ ([[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The Kauffman bracket chart has the over-strand from southwest to northeast, its A-smoothing joins left endpoints, its B-smoothing joins top endpoints, and the loop value is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The positive Artin half twist has label $i$ pass below the midpoint and label $i+1$ pass above, and its over/under projected tangents are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$ in the stated projection coordinates ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text: [F7] The braid exponent sum is a homomorphism with $w(\sigma_i^{\pm1})=\pm1$ ([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, selects an element from every countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

facts.label: F8

steps.text: The element $A^{-4}+1$ is a unit in $R_A$ and $\delta=-A^2(A^{-4}+1)$ is therefore a unit. Set $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. By [F7], $\tau_n(1)=1$, $\tau_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\tau_n(x)$, and $\tau_n$ is cyclic. Since $S_n=-I-qe_n$, the last closure rule of [F7] gives $$\tau_{n+1}((x\otimes1)S_n) =-\tau_n(x)-q\delta^{-1}\tau_n(x) =-\frac{1}{q^2+1}\tau_n(x)=z_0\tau_n(x).$$ Thus $\tau\circ\rho_H$ satisfies all specialized Markov-trace rules, where $\rho_H(T_i)=S_i$. steps.text: Any specialized Markov trace is determined by its restriction to $H(n)$: on $H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus H(n)T_nH(n)$, restriction determines the first summand, while cyclicity and the Markov rule force $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_ny)=z_0\operatorname{tr}_n(yx)$ on every product in the second summand. steps.text: Expand each crossing of $\beta$ by $C_i$ or $C_i^{-}$ and close the resulting Temperley–Lieb diagrams. steps.text: The closure of the identity in $B_1$ has one circle; the state sum gives $\delta^{1-1}=1$, and its trace expression gives $\delta^0(-A)^0\operatorname{tr}_1(1)=1$. facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] A crossing in the source chart is the A-smoothing with coefficient $A$
plus the B-smoothing with coefficient $A^{-1}$, and the loop value is
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$
([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The positive geometric half twist has the explicit diamond path with label
$i$ passing below the midpoint and label $i+1$ above it; the reflected path is
its inverse ([[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text:
[F3] $B_n$ is generated by $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{n-1}$ with the Artin
braid and distant-commutation relations, and the closure joins corresponding
top and bottom endpoints with the strand orientations respected
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text:
[F4] The vertical identity diagram has $n$ through strands; $e_i$ has a top
cap and bottom cup at positions $i,i+1$; stacking removes each closed loop
with coefficient $\delta$
([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] The generators satisfy $e_i^2=\delta e_i$,
$e_ie_{i+1}e_i=e_i$, $e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}=e_{i+1}$, and distant commutation
([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] The local crossing operators satisfy R2 cancellation and the R3 braid
identity in the declared source chart
([[lem-kauffman-bracket-r2-r3-identities]]).

facts.label: F7
facts.text:
[F7] The unnormalized diagram closure trace is cyclic,
$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$, and
$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)e_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$;
when $\delta$ is a unit, $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$
([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]],
[[lem-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-component-identities]]).

facts.label: F8
facts.text:
[F8] The Hecke tower has quadratic relation
$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, and its Ocneanu trace satisfies the tower restriction,
cyclicity, and $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$
([[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]],
[[thm-the-ocneanu-markov-trace-exists-and-is-unique]]).

facts.label: F9
facts.text:
[F9] The assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto T_i$ is a group homomorphism to Hecke
units, and $T_i^{-1}=v^{-1}T_i+(v^{-1}-1)$
([[lem-the-hecke-generators-satisfy-the-artin-relations-and-are-units]]).

facts.label: F10
facts.text:
[F10] The Hecke tower has the decomposition
$H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus H(n)T_nH(n)$ as an $H(n)$-bimodule
([[lem-the-hecke-tower-is-free-over-the-previous-level]]).

facts.label: F11
facts.text:
[F11] The exponent sum is a homomorphism $e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ with
$e(\sigma_i)=1$ ([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

steps.text: Near the three-strand event, choose a linear longitudinal coordinate nonzero on each of the three tangent lines, shrink the event disk, and orient the unoriented local tracks in its increasing direction. All three tracks are then monotone; these temporary arrows do not affect the bracket. Label the tracks $1,2,3$ at the incoming end. The two R3 sides meet their pairs in orders $(12,13,23)$ and $(23,13,12)$, and a strict height order permits exactly the exponent triples $+++, --- , ++-, -++, +--, --+$. The triples $+-+$ and $-+-$ would require a cyclic height order. Put $a=C_i$ and $b=C_{i+1}$. Besides $aba=bab$ from step 1.2 and its inverse from step 1.1, the four needed identities are $$ab a^{-1}=b^{-1}ab,\qquad a^{-1}ba=bab^{-1},\qquad ab^{-1}a^{-1}=b^{-1}a^{-1}b,\qquad a^{-1}b^{-1}a=ba^{-1}b^{-1}.$$ The first follows by multiplying $aba=bab$ on the left by $b^{-1}$ and on the right by $a^{-1}$; the second follows by multiplying on the left by $a^{-1}$ and on the right by $b^{-1}$; the last two are their inverses. Thus each of the six height orders gives equality with exactly its actual over/under choices. For R2, choose a longitudinal coordinate along the common tangent at the bigon event, shrink the disk, and temporarily orient both tracks increasingly; the two local crossings have opposite types and cancel by step 1.1. Reversing any original strand arrow leaves all smoothing weights unchanged. Tensoring or stacking with the unchanged exterior preserves each equality by bilinearity and associativity, proving every R2/R3 variant. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] In the source crossing chart, the A-smoothing has weight $A$, the B-smoothing has weight $A^{-1}$, and a closed trivial loop has value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] The identity $I$ is the vertical through tangle; $e_i$ is the cap on top and cup on bottom, stacking removes loops with coefficient $\delta$, and the stacking product is associative and bilinear ([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], [[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] The generators satisfy $e_i^2=\delta e_i$, $e_ie_{i+1}e_i=e_i$, $e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}=e_{i+1}$, and distant generators commute ([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] R2 creates or deletes two opposite crossings, and every allowed R3 has a strict height order with the cyclic over/under pattern excluded ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

steps.text: First calculate the A-first cube with overpassing order $c>a>b$. The specified curves have exactly three transverse crossings: $r=a\cap b$, $p=c\cap b$ and $q=c\cap a$. In the left diagram $p$ is the upper-right crossing and $q$ the upper-left crossing. Order the crossings $(r,p,q)$. Use the following five pairings: $A=(16)(25)(34)$, $B=(12)(34)(56)$, $C=(16)(23)(45)$, $D=(14)(23)(56)$ and $P=(12)(36)(45)$. The left smoothing table, with rows indexed by $(p,q)$ and columns by $r$, is $00:(C,A)$, $01:(P,B)$, $10:(C\sqcup O,C)$ and $11:(C,D)$. Here $O$ is one interior circle. To verify the table directly, at the left crossing $q$ the $0$ smoothing connects endpoint $1$ to the branch towards $6$; at $p$, the $0$ smoothing connects endpoint $2$ to the branch of $c$ travelling towards $q$. At $r$, its $0$ smoothing connects the two upper diagonal branches and its other pair joins the branches towards $4,5$. Hence the all-zero state is $(16)(23)(45)$. Flipping $q$ alone reconnects $16,23$ into $12,36$, giving $P$; flipping $p$ alone cuts a circle from the path joining $2,3$; flipping $r$ alone reconnects $23,45$ into $25,34$, giving $A$. With $r=1$, flipping $q$ then joins the pairs to give $B$, flipping $p$ removes the just-described circle to give $C$, and flipping both gives $D$. With $r=0$, flipping $p,q$ merges that circle into the other arc and returns $C$. These traces specify the actual crossing disks and the saddle bands at their flips. [F1, F6, given, construct]

steps.text: The second geometric variant, with overpassing order $c>b>a$, is obtained by reflecting the first across the vertical diameter. This sends $a$ to $b$, preserves each upward or downward bow of $c$, and changes the crossing between the diagonals to $b$ over $a$, exactly as required. At every crossing reflection changes a right turn into a left turn, so it interchanges its $0$ and $1$ smoothings. It follows that its actual raw cube is the reflected, time-reversed-surface dual of the first cube with all three bits complemented. A vertex of old degree $s$ becomes degree $3-s$ and has shift $3-s$, obtained from its dual shift $-s$ by adding three. steps.text: To obtain the B-first maps, use surface-time duality on the raw cubes, without changing the projection diagram. steps.text: Put $q=c+m+1\ge2$. For a state, let $\beta$ pair the two left and two right ports for A, or the two top and two bottom ports for B. steps.text: For a positive curl, the local differential is $(u,v)\mapsto u+Xv$ from the small-circle coordinates $1\otimes u+X\otimes v$ to the continuing arc. Change coordinates to $(u',v')=(u+Xv,v)$. The retraction has inclusion $i(w)=(0,w)$, projection $p(u',v')=v'$, and contraction $h(w)=(w,0)$ on the target; hence $pi=1$ and $1-ip=dh+hd$. For a negative curl, the local differential is $v\mapsto(Xv,v)$ into the small-circle coordinates. Change target coordinates to $(w'_1,w_X)=(w_1-Xw_X,w_X)$; then the map is $v\mapsto(0,v)$, and the retraction onto $w'_1$ has inclusion $i(w)=(w,0)$, projection $p(w'_1,w_X)=w'_1$, and contraction $h(0,w) = w$ from the $w_X$ target summand to the source. These formulas give $pi=1$ and $1-ip=dh+hd$. Before the writhe shifts, the positive survivor has quantum shift $-1$ and the negative survivor has quantum shift $+2$; the new $+1$ and $-2$ writhe shifts cancel them, respectively. In both cases the normalized homological degree agrees with the original. For Reidemeister II use the local maps $i(v)=(v,tv,0)$ and $p(v,w_1,w_X)=v-sw_X$ from [F3]; the identity $ts=x+y$ used in $dh+hd=1-ip$ is exactly the second identity in step 1.1. Its local homological and quantum shifts are canceled by the one positive and one negative crossing normalization changes. For Reidemeister III, the two cancellations in [F4] use only identity pivots and the same split coordinates, while writhe normalization is unchanged. All coordinate changes have pivots $\pm1$ and entries given by the Lee saddle and dot maps, so they preserve the decreasing filtration after normalization. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

facts.label: F2

facts.label: F6

steps.text:
Order crossings from top to bottom. The first differential sends $1\otimes1$ to $(1,1,1)$ and $1\otimes X$ to zero, so its image is the diagonal copy of $\mathbb Z$ and its kernel is $\mathbb Z\{1\otimes X\}$. After suppressing the common based factor $M$, the next differential is the signed incidence matrix
$$
\begin{pmatrix}-1&1&0\\-1&0&1\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}
$$
with each integer entry multiplying the label $X$, because each edge splits the based circle and the reduced split sends $1$ to $1\otimes X$. Its image has rank two and its kernel is the diagonal copy of $\mathbb Z$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

Label the three two-circle states in crossing order and identify the two unbased factors in the all-$B$ state from left to right. The last differential is
$$
(a,b,c)\longmapsto a\otimes X-\Delta(b)+X\otimes c.
$$
Here the first and third edges split the based circle, while the middle edge splits the unbased circle; the signs are the cube signs from [F2]. Its image is exactly the subgroup generated by $1\otimes X$, $X\otimes1$, and $X\otimes X$, and its kernel consists of triples with equal coefficients of $1$ and with coefficients of $X$ satisfying $a_X-b_X+c_X=0$. steps.text: Now return to the specified negative diagram. At each crossing its A-smoothing is cap-cup and its B-smoothing is through, so the state $v$ has exactly the same circles as the auxiliary positive state $w=1-v$. steps.text: The bilinear map $B$ and vector $U(1)$ are $U_{q_K}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ intertwiners. The $K_K$-weights in each nonzero pairing and coevaluation term multiply to $1$. facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] The Drinfeld–Jimbo presentation has $K E K^{-1}=q^2E$, $K F K^{-1}=q^{-2}F$, and $EF-FE=(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ case ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] In the library convention, $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K\otimes F$, and the antipode is $S(E)=-EK$, $S(F)=-K^{-1}F$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] A braiding is a natural isomorphism $c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\to Y\otimes X$ satisfying the two hexagon identities ([[def-braiding]]).

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] A ribbon twist is a natural automorphism satisfying $\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and compatible with duality ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]).

facts.label: F5

facts.label: F6

facts.label: F7

The positive raw differential is $(a,b)\mapsto a+xb$. Set $i(v)=(-xv,v)$, $p(a,b)=b$, and $h(v)=(v,0)$ from degree one to degree zero. Then $pi=1$, $di=0$, and on degree zero $1-ip$ sends $(a,b)$ to $(a+xb,0)=hd(a,b)$; on degree one $dh=1$. facts.text: [F1] The branched cover is well-defined up to oriented diffeomorphism ([[lem-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link-well-defined]]).

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] For a fixed diagram, the surgery construction has $E_2$ equal to based reduced Khovanov cohomology and converges to the branched-cover Floer group ([[thm-os-spectral-sequence-for-a-fixed-link-diagram]]).

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] Over ACω, the reduced Khovanov group is independent of the chosen diagram and marked component up to bigraded isomorphism ([[thm-reduced-khovanov-over-f2-link-invariance]]).

facts.label: A1
facts.text: [A1] AC is used by the link-complement and covering-space construction; ACω is separately used by the Reidemeister-move and generic Floer analytic branches ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]).
